newsitem.title: CANADA: Merged Northstar, Morrison may sell production.
newsitem.headline: Merged Northstar, Morrison may sell production.

text.p: Northstar Energy Corp and Morrison Petroleums Ltd, which earlier announced a merger deal, said combined production would be about 42,500 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
However, after the deal closes, the merged firm would likely sell 2,000 to 4,000 barrels per day to "fine tune the assets," Northstar chairman John Hagg said in a conference call on Thursday.
In a day in Canada's energy sector that could only be described as an investment banker's dream, Northstar and Morrison said they planned to merge in a share-swap deal valued at about C$700 million.

The deal followed Talisman Energy Inc.'s huge takeover offer for Wascana Energy Inc and another merger announced by Newport Petroleum Corp and Cimarron Petroleum Ltd. Both were made public late Wedensday.
Under the deal, the merged firm, to retain the Northstar name, would produce about equal proportions of gas and oil.
Hagg said the operational fit of Northstar and Morrison was "just excellent."

"We have six principal core areas in which Morrison is a direct overlap with four of those, "he said. "It's going to cut costs for us, it's going to increase our efficiencies in terms of both exploration and development, it's going to make us a more dominant player in those areas."
Company officials said the new firm would dominate vast tracts of shallow natural gas lands in northern Alberta.
The merged firm was expected to have a debt-to-cash flow ratio of 1.5 times following the deal and a share buyback.
Morrison chief executive Gordon Stollery said he and Hagg had discussed the possibilities of merging before Canadian 88 Energy Corp launched its failed hostile bid for Morrison in early January.
Stollery also said Northstar was not Morrison's only prospective suitor. "There was one other written bid and some other verbal indications," he said.

Company officials said they would mount a roadshow through Canada's major financial centers starting on Monday to sell investors on the friendly deal, which was recommended by both boards of directors.
Canadian 88 withdrew its offer for Morrison last weekend amid mounting uncertainty over alleged regulatory improprieties.
